LESSON: READING 1.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell how a story, poem or conversation will end? 2. Why is it important to identify the main idea in a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they argue out their own points during group discussion.

Values:
Respect: A learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they answer the comprehension questions correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the comprehension strategies in reading of texts in other Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
